chunks: There was a wife with me who practiced this matter (al-wilayah), and her father was likewise, and she was of evil character. So I abhorred divorcing her due to my recognition of her faith and the faith of her father. So I met Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), while I intended to ask him about divorcing her. So I said: May I be made a ransom for you! Indeed, for me there is a need to you, so permit me to ask you about it. So he said: Come to me tomorrow at the Zuhr prayer.

He said: So when I had prayed the Zuhr, I came to him and found him having already prayed and seated. So I entered to him and sat before him. He began speaking to me first and said: O Khattab! My father had married me to a daughter of a paternal uncle of mine, and she was of evil character; and sometimes my father would lock the door upon me and upon her, hoping that I would meet her. So I would climb the wall and flee from her. So when my father passed away, I divorced her.
So I said: Allah is Greatest! By Allah, He has answered me about my need without being asked.

key_terms.الْأَمْرَ: al-amr — the 'matter', here referring to al-wilayah (the authority/guardianship of the Imams), a term used in early Shia tradition to describe commitment to the Imamate
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: juiltu fidak — a formulaic expression of extreme reverence meaning 'may I be made a ransom/sacrifice for you', used when addressing Imams
key_terms.سَيِّئَةَ الْخُلُقِ: sayyi'at al-khuluq — 'of evil character/manners', the description used for the incompatible wife in both Khattab's and the Imam's case
key_terms.صَلَاةَ الظُّهْرِ: salat al-Zuhr — the noon prayer, one of the five daily obligatory prayers in Islam

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia Islam to divorce a believing wife because of bad character?
ai.summary: Khattab ibn Salama narrates that he had a wife of evil character who was nonetheless a faithful believer; he therefore hesitated to divorce her. When he sought to consult Imam al-Kazim (AS) on this matter, the Imam preemptively shared his own personal experience: that his father Imam al-Sadiq (AS) had similarly arranged a marriage for him with a difficult cousin, from whom he finally divorced after his father's death. The hadith establishes that even the Imams endured the strain of incompatible marriages and that divorce is a valid recourse when a spouse's character makes cohabitation untenable, even if the spouse is a believer.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ibrahim Bin Is’haq Al Ahmar, from Abdullah Bin Hammad, from Khattab Bin Salma who said, ‘There was a wife with me described upon this matter (Al-Wilayah), and her father was like that, and she was of evil manners. But, I abhorred divorcing her due to my recognition of her faith and the faith of her father. So I met Abu Al-Hassan Musaasws, and I intended to ask himasws about divorcing her. So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you! For me there is a need to youasws’. So heasws permitted me that I ask himasws about her, and heasws said: ‘Come to measws tomorrow at Al-Zohr Prayer’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So when I had Prayed Al-Zohr, I found himasws (also) to have Prayed, and seated. So I went over to himasws and sat in front of him. He began before me, so heasws said: ‘O Khattab! Myasws fatherasws got measws married to a daughter of an uncle of mineasws, and she was of evil manners; and sometimes myasws fatherasws used to lock the door upon measws and upon her, hoping that Iasws settle (my affairs) with her. So Iasws would climb the wall and go away from her. So when myasws fatherasws passed away, Iasws divorced her’.
So I said, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the Greatest! You<sup>asws</sup> have answered me, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, from my need, without being asked’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn has narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar from ‘Abd Allah ibn Hammad Khattab ibn Salmah who has said the following: “I had a wife who believed (in the divine authority of ‘ A’immah ) and so also was her father, but she had very bad moral behaviors and I did not like to divorce her because of her belief and the belief of her father. I met abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and I wanted to ask him (the Imam) if divorcing her is proper saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I need an answer to a question and I like to ask you.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Come tomorrow at the time of al- Zuhr Salat (prayer).

He (the narrator) has said, ‘After performing al-Zuhr Salat (prayer) I went to see him (the Imam) and I found that he (the Imam) had completed his Salat (prayer) and he was sitting. I went inside and sat in front of him (the Imam). He (the Imam) initiated speaking to me and said, ‘O Khattab, my father made me marry a daughter of my uncle and her moral behaviors were very bad. My father sometimes would close the door on both of us in the hope that I may meet her, instead of climbing the wall to run away. When my father passed away I divorced her.’
I (the narrator) then said to myself, ‘Allah is Greater than can be described, He (the Imam) has answered my question before I could even ask him (the Imam).”’
